item.title: ‘Beautiful, smart, fun-loving, energetic’: Ocala community holds a vigil for 3-year-old girl
item.description: Ocala community members organized a vigil in downtown Ocala where dozens gathered Thursday night to honor 3-year-old Paisley Brown just one week after police say she was killed by her mother’s boyfriend.

item.title: Dentists and veterinarians team up to treat monkeys at Gainesville sanctuary
item.description: The Saturday morning quiet quickly turned into a chorus of monkey screams as the Jungle Friends Primate Sanctuary turned its clinic into a dental suite in partnership with the Dental Coalition for Conservation.

item.title: Florida bill targeting sexual content in books sparks concern in Alachua County
item.description: Supporters of the bill say it strengthens parental rights and ensures children are not exposed to inappropriate material. Critics argue the language is broad and could lead to the removal of a wide range of books, including works often taught in high school literature classes.

item.title: The anatomy of becoming: Identity and resilience shape a Latina dance senior’s capstone at UF
item.description: As a first-generation American, the BFA dance senior channels the resilience and hard work taught by her Hispanic parents into her nature vs. nurture capstone.

item.title: Alachua County’s new school zoning maps set stage for possible March vote, critics call for alternatives
item.description: Alachua County Public Schools administrators anticipate a final draft of the new school zoning map to be ready sometime mid-March, according to ACPS director of communications, Jackie Johnson.

item.title: Florida's warming trend, rain chances & rip current risk
item.description: Constant eastward wind flow will keep humidity levels present across parts of Florida. This also increases the risk of rip currents along Florida's east coast.

item.title: Q&A: Dandelion Project founder & Executive Director Lisa Bolton
item.description: Since its official start in 2023, the project has offered resources to grieving families in north central Florida, including the recent addition of a ‘wind phone’ at Highland Memorial Park.

item.title: Dunnellon considers legal action against CSX
item.description: The Dunnellon City Council is considering legal action against businesses connected to February's rail tie fire.

item.title: Florida Senate passes bill to add local control over data centers
item.description: The Florida Senate passed a bill on Thursday that would increase transparency and local control over data center facilities.

item.title: See how warm and dry spring could be
item.description: NOAA forecasters believe the current La Niña state will transition into an ENSO-neutral pattern. Meteorological spring runs from March 1 through May 31.
